checklist_items.1.1: Product name, header title, and sign-in page text are textboxes. None is required. Each opens empty, with no unit. Their maximum lengths are 32, 64, and 200. Their placeholders are GPUWorks, the built-in header title, and the built-in sign-in text. The logo is a file input that accepts image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, and image/svg+xml. It is not required, it has no unit, and the restore control stays hidden while the stored logo is empty. All four fields stay visible. Reading them sends no PATCH. The independent GET of the untouched card is product_name, console_title, login_description, and logo, each empty. The save body uses those same four fields, and the independent GET persists the saved values. After a logo is set, the restore control is visible
checklist_items.1.2: covered: While the branding GET is held the Save button stays disabled, then the empty defaults appear. Reload backfills every saved field, and the card has no secret input
checklist_items.1.7: Saving the card reaches the exact PATCH body for all four fields
checklist_items.1.8: covered: The save PATCH and the reload plus independent GET match product name, console title, login description and logo; the initial GET and the cleared save are the empty backend defaults
checklist_items.1.9: covered: While the branding PATCH is held a second click and Enter send no further save, and the later 200 is the only stored branding
checklist_items.1.10: A control character in the product name keeps the branding card open. This card is not a dialog. The sign-in description textarea has an inline height while the card is empty, and it still has an inline height after the rejection. The server returns 400 with code FIELD_INVALID. The product name draft stays the rejected value. The header stays the previously saved name. The independent GET stays on that saved name with an empty console title, an empty login description, and an empty logo. The visible reason is the localized save-failed sentence around the localized invalid-value sentence and the server detail that the product name contains a control character. Filling the 32-character product name and saving returns 200, the header matches those 32 characters, and the independent GET stores that name.
checklist_items.1.12: The branding card has no switch. The logo control is one upload. Changing only the product name from AlphaName to BetaName keeps an empty header title, an empty sign-in description, and an empty logo. Each of those saves returns 200 and the independent GET matches. Saving the sign-in description Sign-in line and then clearing it keeps BetaName, the empty header title, and the empty logo. Setting one logo, replacing it with a second logo, and restoring the logo to empty each return 200. Each independent GET keeps BetaName, the empty header title, and the empty sign-in description, and the stored logo matches that step. The closing save stores the four empty fields and the independent GET matches.
checklist_items.1.13: While the branding card is open on the empty draft, another session's PATCH of product name Other Session, header title Other Title, sign-in text Other line, and an empty logo returns 200. The independent GET is that branding. The card still shows the empty product name, header title, and sign-in text, and it shows no logo. There is no conflict status. Saving that draft returns 200 with the four empty fields, and the independent GET returns those empty fields
checklist_items.1.14: Reload and independent GET preserve the branding; the public sign-in page agrees
checklist_items.1.15: The product name shows the count 0 / 32. Tab from the upload button reaches the product name, then the header title, then the sign-in description. Save in the card header can be focused. Enter in the empty product name sends no branding PATCH and the value stays empty. A control character then shows the localized save-failed sentence. At 1440×900 the product name, the header title, the sign-in description, and Save are each inside the viewport, and the product name does not overlap Save.
checklist_items.2.1: Labels, defaults and the empty values are asserted before editing
checklist_items.2.2: Multiline sign-in text is persisted and shown on the public page
checklist_items.2.3: Empty is the shortest product name and the closing save stores it. There is no shorter value. The control stops at 32 Unicode characters, the header and the independent GET match those 32 characters, and a 33-character PATCH returns FIELD_INVALID while the stored name stays at 32. Thirty-two Chinese characters are accepted, so the limit counts characters rather than UTF-8 bytes
checklist_items.2.4: The product name saves Chinese, English, a digit and punctuation. The header and the independent GET match that saved value. A control character in the product name returns FIELD_INVALID, the field keeps that rejected draft, and the independent GET stays on the saved name. The login description saves an internal newline and the independent GET keeps that newline
checklist_items.2.6: The login description accepts a pasted 粘A1., a keyboard clear back to empty, and keyboard editing that includes an internal newline. That newline is the saved PATCH value. Reload and the independent GET keep it. Paste, clear and typing send no request of their own
checklist_items.16.1: The upload rejects a non-image type and accepts a real image; size/type boundaries remain MISSING
checklist_items.2.7: The product name is free text, so it can carry markup. 'e2e--brand' is saved through the real PATCH, the independent GET confirms the server holds that exact string, and the edit control still shows it verbatim. The public sign-in page then displays it as a text node whose element has no child elements, its document title equals the raw string, and no img[src=x] element exists there or on the settings page. The name is restored afterwards so the recorded evidence matches the original brand. Proven by mutation: rendering the name with dangerouslySetInnerHTML on the sign-in page makes the case fail.
checklist_items.2.5: A real conflict against server state is constructed, though not a uniqueness conflict: branding has no name uniqueness to violate (it is a single row under one setting key, replaced without lookup or comparison), so the conflict used here is a concurrent writer. exercise_branding_conflict PATCHes the branding from a second session, asserts through the independent GET that the other session won and is what the server holds, then asserts that the open card kept its own draft - the four fields still read the card's values, the header fell back to the built-in wordmark rather than showing the other session's empty logo, and the card shows no error. Saving the open draft is then asserted to PATCH exactly the draft and to become what a fresh GET returns, so the conflict is resolved by a successful resubmit. The other session's write is asserted not to be counted as a page save. No mutation was performed for this item: the product reaches the draft through local React state, and two attempts to make the card read server state instead (a periodic refresh, and binding the field to the shared store) either fell outside the assertion window or could not be reached by a second session's PATCH, so the discriminating power here is not demonstrated by a product mutation. What it does have is an independent check: the other session's write is confirmed through a fresh GET, and the open draft is confirmed to be what a later PATCH sends and what a later GET returns.
